books.title: Clean Code
books.author: Robert C. Martin
books.description: Clean Code is a guide to writing software that other people can read, understand and safely change. Robert C. Martin argues that code is read far more often than it is written, so clarity should be a programmer's first priority. The book walks through practical advice on naming variables and functions, keeping functions small and focused, writing useful comments (and avoiding useless ones), handling errors cleanly and formatting code consistently. It also includes a long case study in which messy code is cleaned up step by step, and a closing catalogue of "smells" that signal when code needs improving. It is written for working programmers and students who want to build good habits early, and most of its examples are in Java.

books.title: Design Patterns
books.author: Gang of Four
books.description: Design Patterns introduced the idea of reusable solutions to common problems in object-oriented software design. The authors, often called the "Gang of Four", describe 23 patterns grouped into three families: creational patterns (how objects are created, such as Singleton and Factory), structural patterns (how objects are combined, such as Adapter and Decorator) and behavioural patterns (how objects communicate, such as Observer and Strategy). Each pattern is explained with its purpose, structure, a worked example and the trade-offs of using it. The book also gave developers a shared vocabulary that is still used today when discussing design. It works best as a reference for readers who already have some experience with object-oriented programming.

books.title: Introduction to Algorithms
books.author: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein
books.description: Introduction to Algorithms, widely known as CLRS after its authors, is one of the most used textbooks on algorithms. It starts with the foundations, including how to analyse an algorithm's running time and memory use, and then covers major topics such as sorting and searching, data structures like heaps, hash tables and balanced trees, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph algorithms (shortest paths, spanning trees, network flow) and NP-completeness. Each algorithm is given in pseudocode, explained in plain language and supported by mathematical proof. It suits university students and anyone preparing for exams, competitive programming or technical interviews. Because it is rigorous, it is best studied slowly, chapter by chapter, together with the exercises.

books.title: Head First Design Patterns
books.author: Freeman & Robson
books.description: Head First Design Patterns teaches the same ideas as the classic design patterns book, but in a far more visual and conversational style. Instead of dense theory, it uses stories, diagrams, puzzles, quizzes and humour to help the concepts stick. Readers learn patterns such as Strategy, Observer, Decorator, Factory, Singleton, Command and Adapter by following a problem, seeing why a simple solution falls short, and then improving it with the pattern. Along the way it introduces core object-oriented design principles, such as favouring composition over inheritance and programming to interfaces rather than implementations. The examples are written in Java. It is a friendly first book on the subject for beginners and intermediate programmers.

books.title: Building Microservices
books.author: Sam Newman
books.description: Building Microservices explains how to design systems as a collection of small, independently deployable services instead of one large application. It covers how to split a system into services, how those services communicate with each other, how to deploy and test them, and how to monitor them once they are running. It also discusses security, scaling, resilience and the way team structure affects architecture. The author is honest about the downsides, such as the extra complexity that comes with distributed systems, and helps readers decide when microservices are the right choice and when they are not. It is aimed at developers, architects and technical leads working on large or growing systems.

books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
books.author: Andrew Hunt, David Thomas
books.description: The Pragmatic Programmer is a collection of practical advice on becoming a better software developer. Rather than focusing on one language or tool, it covers the habits and mindset behind good work: taking responsibility for your code, not repeating yourself (the DRY principle), keeping designs flexible, writing tests, debugging methodically and automating repetitive tasks. It also discusses working with teams, making estimates and continuing to learn throughout a career. The advice is presented as short, numbered tips with everyday analogies, so the book can be read in any order. The second edition updates the examples for modern development. It suits both beginners and experienced developers.

books.title: Python Crash Course
books.author: Eric Matthes
books.description: Python Crash Course is a hands-on introduction to programming for complete beginners. The first part teaches the fundamentals of Python, including variables, lists, loops, conditions, functions, classes, files and exceptions, with clear explanations and short exercises. The second part puts those skills to work through three projects: a simple arcade-style game built with Pygame, data visualisations made with libraries such as Matplotlib, and a small web application built with Django. By the end, readers have a solid grounding in the language and finished projects to show for it. It is a good starting point for students and self-taught learners.

books.author: George Orwell
books.description: 1984 is a dystopian novel by George Orwell set in a future society ruled by a totalitarian government called the Party and its leader, Big Brother. The story follows Winston Smith, a low-ranking worker whose job is to rewrite historical records so that they match whatever the Party currently claims. Citizens are watched constantly through telescreens, and even private thoughts can be punished as crimes. Winston begins to rebel in secret, keeping a diary and starting a forbidden relationship, but he soon learns how far the Party will go to control people. The book explores surveillance, propaganda, the manipulation of truth and the loss of individual freedom. Terms from it, such as "Big Brother" and "doublethink", have entered everyday language.

books.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.description: Sapiens is a broad history of the human species, from the first appearance of Homo sapiens in Africa to the present day. Yuval Noah Harari divides the story into major turning points: the Cognitive Revolution, which let humans share stories and cooperate in large groups; the Agricultural Revolution, which changed how people lived and worked; the unification of humankind through money, empires and religion; and the Scientific Revolution, which transformed knowledge and power. Throughout, he asks big questions about happiness, inequality and the kind of future humans are creating. It is written for general readers and mixes history, biology and philosophy. Some of its interpretations are debated, which makes it good for discussion.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.description: Atomic Habits is a practical guide to changing behaviour through small, consistent improvements. James Clear explains that habits follow a simple loop of cue, craving, response and reward, and that lasting change comes from adjusting each step rather than relying on willpower alone. He offers four laws for building good habits (make it obvious, make it attractive, make it easy and make it satisfying) and the reverse for breaking bad ones. The book also stresses focusing on identity, becoming the kind of person who does something, rather than only on goals, and shows how tiny daily gains add up over time. It uses real stories from sport, business and everyday life and is easy to apply.
